suites.title: Backend and executable origin
suites.contract: Only a validated trusted backend/executable identity may run before confinement; backend failure never widens authority.
attempts: Try to make an inert launch plan choose a workspace search entry instead of its trusted absolute backend.
Vary mocked executable ownership, alias identity, replacement epoch, helper override, and startup-hook environment.
Remove or mismatch the backend in a fake launcher and check that no FULL_ACCESS retry is requested.
suites.mutation: Substitute PATH lookup for a trusted absolute backend, remove ownership checks, or add an unsandboxed fallback in a pure launch-plan mutant.
suites.limit: No replacement backend, shell startup hook, package script, dependency binary, or downloaded program is executed. Provenance/supply-chain compromise beyond the modeled origin contract remains static.

suites.title: Git metadata and mount authority
suites.contract: Repository metadata must never create new host read authority; protected metadata must remain immutable under the specified project contract.
attempts: Make a synthetic .git pointer refer to the forbidden sibling fixture and inspect the parsed Linux mount graph.
Vary relative pointers, missing targets, aliases, duplicate roots, nested .git directories, and inert commondir/bare-repository descriptions.

For separately registered native cases, attempt only one marker creation in an existing fixture .git directory or one synthetic-history canary read; never invoke real Git tooling or mutate repository metadata.
suites.mutation: Add an unapproved sibling target to a fake mount graph or omit one metadata write protection; require the corresponding authority oracle to detect it.
suites.limit: Pointer-derived mount expansion is policy/fixture-only until independently reviewed; no native F2 escape attempt. New/aliased Git layouts are simulated unless a registered fixed fixture case exists.

suites.title: Path identity, roots, and read grants
suites.contract: Canonical roots and additional grants stay within explicitly approved authority; sensitive/trusted overlap is rejected in either direction.
attempts: Represent traversal, prefix collisions, broad ancestors, and aliases with fixture object IDs; dangerous host roots exist only in a fake filesystem.
Vary roots above and below synthetic sensitive directories and compare macOS policy and Linux mount intentions independently.
Use a single synthetic sibling read or exclusive marker for admitted deterministic native path cases; model renames, changing mounts, and races as scheduled fake-filesystem events.
suites.mutation: Emit a fixture-ancestor PATH read grant, remove reverse-overlap rejection, or accept a stale directory identity in a mock plan.
suites.limit: No live mount operations, FUSE, network filesystems, ancestor renames, TOCTOU races, or path probes outside the fixture. Runtime filename semantics remain platform-specific.

suites.title: Synthetic secret confidentiality
suites.contract: The documented sensitive-content boundary must cover every exposure route it claims, and no forbidden synthetic bytes may appear in child output.
attempts: Place synthetic values in small conventional secret-name and generated-directory fixtures; vary suffix case and exempt-name assumptions without using real secret material.
Model or precreate a hard-link alias whose two names and inode are both owned by the fixture; try only the registered single read.
Simulate a file appearing after policy construction and require an explicit rejection, policy refresh, or recorded confidentiality limitation.
Distinguish macOS denial from Linux empty masking, with independent positive reads proving the probe works.
suites.mutation: Remove one deny/mask or alias guard from a fake authority plan and check the canary oracle catches disclosure.
suites.limit: No real credentials, home copies, Git secrets, concurrent tree mutation, or canary values in agent reports. Arbitrary content classification is not solved by filename tests.

suites.title: Approval scope, persistence, and revocation
suites.contract: Approval must remain tied to its declared scope and explicit authority; failed persistence, changed membership, or revocation must not silently preserve broader grants.
attempts: Reuse the same inert command text under different directories, scripts, root sets, and background intent and inspect authorization decisions.
Change a fake workspace manifest while retaining its pathname and verify old grants are reauthorized or invalidated.
Inject save/load failures, invalid policy ownership, and revocation through fake stores; verify no permission widening or fallback.
Check multi-root display and persistent FULL_ACCESS decisions with fake presenters only.
suites.mutation: Ignore root membership, retain a failed-save in-memory grant, or map a denial to FULL_ACCESS in fake authorization state.
suites.limit: Never change real permissions, workspace manifests, persisted account state, or user policy files. No actual FULL_ACCESS command is launched.

suites.title: Terminal ownership and authority lifetime
suites.contract: Terminal actions are owner-bound and carry explicit process authority; input and automatic wake cannot bypass that capability contract.
attempts: Create fake actors A and B and let B know A terminal ID; check list/read/input/close/reuse/wake authorization independently.
Feed inert stdin tokens to a fake interpreter process and ensure authority is recorded and checked for later input.
Schedule cancellation, immediate-child exit, timeout, and delayed descendant completion using fake process objects and clocks.
suites.mutation: Remove one owner check or bypass the interactive authority check; model an early child-exit return that leaves cleanup incomplete.
suites.limit: No actual interactive interpreter, FULL_ACCESS process, detached child, daemon, process-group manipulation, persistence, or termination evasion. Live descendant-escape claims remain unverified.

suites.title: Trusted installation and trace writer
suites.contract: Trusted launch/build inputs and trace destinations must not be controlled by writable projects; host writer identity must remain stable.
attempts: Build a synthetic installation/workspace graph and vary overlap of source, dependencies, executables, and build inputs.
Configure a fake trace inside, below, or aliased into a writable project; require rejection before logging.
Model replacement between checked destination and append/chmod as fake filesystem events and observe attempted authority, without performing deputy writes.
suites.mutation: Accept a writable installation or trace destination, or reopen a replaced pathname in the mock writer.
suites.limit: Never execute package scripts, rebuild poisoned helpers, launch Glyph from a modified checkout, activate IDE/watchers, redirect a real logger, or chmod a canary. Trusted-deputy exploitation is mock-only.

suites.title: Output, wake events, and presentation
suites.contract: Untrusted output remains data/tool content and cannot acquire developer authority, change approval state, or leak fixture values into agent-facing reports.
attempts: Send inert synthetic instruction-like text through a scripted wake path and inspect captured request roles locally.
Vary split terminal controls, bidi markers, confusables, and long-but-bounded display strings using snapshots, never an actual terminal control channel.
Place a fake sensitive token in mock output and assert the report emitter supplies only approved booleans and IDs.
suites.mutation: Promote wake output to developer role, omit provenance, or forward raw mock output to the agent-report adapter.
suites.limit: No real provider calls, no live prompt-injection success claim, no raw child output to agents, no OSC/terminal device actions. Disable wake/resume/tracing integration during native canaries.

suites.title: Command grammar and policy serialization
suites.contract: The safe classifier never stands in for containment; command data stays separate from backend options and policy syntax.
attempts: Generate at most 100 tiny inert quoting/option/whitespace examples and compare against an independently specified allowed grammar.
Place leading-option and escaped-path byte cases in recording launchers; verify separators and structured argument identity.
Model archive traversal against fixture path IDs without executing an extractor or interpreter.
suites.mutation: Remove a separator, escape rule, or classifier rejection from a pure-data mutant; confirm the test catches the intended interpretation change.
suites.limit: Never pass adversarial command text, expansions, utility execution options, serialized policy injection, or archives to a real shell/backend. Unmodeled dialect behavior is a residual gap.

suites.title: IPC, kernel surface, and loopback denial
suites.contract: Every IPC/syscall/descriptor capability has an explicit bounded rationale; registered loopback cases demonstrate only the stated direct TCP restriction.
attempts: Audit the policy inventory for unexpected Mach services, shared memory, device/descriptor grants, namespace options, and exposed endpoint types using data models.
Model a host broker or inherited capability as an inert capability ID; ask whether the admission policy exposes it, without contacting anything.
For K14 only, propose one numeric fixture-loopback TCP connection with a controlled synthetic response and independent listener observations.
For CVEs, map affected component and prerequisites to supplied advisory/version records and explicitly separate unknown reachability.
suites.mutation: Add an unreviewed capability to a mock policy or fake an unsupported backend as valid; never inject a kernel flaw or real service request.
suites.limit: No Mach/XPC calls, shared-memory enumeration, host sockets, device ioctls, raw sockets, DNS, external traffic, CVE replay, privilege changes, namespaces/mount experiments, or exploit binaries. K14 native allowance does not extend to other K vectors.

suites.title: Bounded work, temporary storage, and metadata
suites.contract: Resource limits and lifecycle/report handling are explicit and independently supervised; fixture cleanup never follows attacker-controlled paths.
attempts: Use small injected limits and fake clocks to exercise boundary-minus-one/boundary/boundary-plus-one values without generating large loads.
Represent recursion, file size, process count, output volume, and backpressure as counters or fake streams.
Check temporary-storage admission and one approved scratch marker as a positive fixture case.
Represent metadata operations, devices, FIFOs, mounts, and side-channel observations as denied symbolic capabilities; do not exercise them on the host.
suites.mutation: Remove a small input/scan bound, return success on timeout, or follow a fake cleanup symlink and require the appropriate safety assertion to fail.
suites.limit: No exhaustion, load tests, fork loops, resource pressure, real metadata/ACL manipulation outside ordinary controller setup, timing side-channel measurements, or live cleanup evasion.

suites.title: Harness, oracle, and evidence integrity
suites.contract: Only an independently observed restriction with valid controls and cleanup earns its declared evidence level; unrun/unsupported/static cells remain explicit.
attempts: Give the fake harness nonzero setup errors, empty masked reads, forged marker strings, truncated reports, crashes, and missing positive controls.
Attempt to submit an unknown case, oversized proposal, foreign fixture slot, unsupported platform, or Astra worker identity; require rejection before execution.
Challenge coverage reports that conflate mocks with native enforcement, count CVEs as exploited, or close findings without regression evidence.
suites.mutation: Turn a skip into pass, accept a marker string without a file, or credit Linux evidence to macOS; require report validation to fail.
suites.limit: Only fake failures and inert outcome records. Do not crash the real backend, kill unrelated processes, or execute a runtime campaign while auditing the plan.

cves.applicability_note: Direct dependency, conditional. Relevant when setup creates objects beneath attacker-controlled filesystem content. Glyph overlays workspace-derived paths during setup, so mount order and destination resolution deserve review. This is a setup flaw, not a claim that an established sandbox can be escaped at runtime.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Bubblewrap setup-time symlink traversal; upstream versions below 0.12.0; fixed in 0.12.0.

cves.applicability_note: Direct dependency, configuration-dependent. Requires the affected setuid deployment; non-setuid operation is not affected by this issue. Glyph does not select or verify installation mode. Privilege-escalation testing is prohibited.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Privileged setup manipulation in setuid Bubblewrap 0.11.x before 0.11.2.

cves.applicability_note: Historical direct-dependency issue. Demonstrates that helper setup and privilege transitions are part of the boundary. No assertion that these obsolete versions are installed or that Glyph's normal arguments trigger it.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Setuid Bubblewrap 0.4.0 combined with enabled unprivileged user namespaces; fixed in 0.4.1.

cves.applicability_note: Mitigated design precedent. Bubblewrap explicitly recommends a new session or syscall filtering for this class. Glyph supplies `--new-session`, detached launch, and pipe stdio. These controls should remain intact.

Integration precedent, not a Glyph dependency finding. Demonstrates hostile command data becoming sandbox configuration. Glyph supplies `--` before the child command, the relevant visible defense. It does not implement this Flatpak portal.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Flatpak portal-to-Bubblewrap argument injection. Fixed Flatpak branches include 1.10.9, 1.12.9, 1.14.6, and 1.15.8.

cves.applicability_note: Integration precedent. Relevant to launcher environments and host brokers, not evidence that Glyph uses the vulnerable portal. The key question is which inputs are trusted before confinement.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Flatpak spawn-portal environment injection into unsandboxed host processes; fixed in 1.10.0 and 1.8.5.

cves.applicability_note: Shared-kernel precedent. Shows why read-only mounts are not a defense against a vulnerable kernel. Applicability requires an affected kernel and reachable primitives; installed kernel/backport status was not checked.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Linux page-cache integrity failure allowing modification of readable files despite read-only access.

cves.applicability_note: Shared-kernel precedent. Relevant to namespace-enabled sandboxes and broad syscall exposure. Requires an affected kernel and the necessary API/capability conditions; not a demonstrated Glyph escape.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: Linux filesystem-context heap overflow, with user namespaces affecting unprivileged reachability.

cves.applicability_note: Broker precedent. Motivates review of host launch services and authorized Mach interactions. Apple application-sandbox conditions must not be assumed identical to this custom Seatbelt profile.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: macOS LaunchServices sandbox restriction bypass; addressed in the cited Big Sur 11.6.6 update.

cves.applicability_note: OS-service precedent. Relevant only if the affected functionality is reachable from the permitted process and IPC surface on an unpatched OS.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: ATS sandbox escape; addressed in Sequoia 15.7.

cves.applicability_note: OS-service/race precedent. A network-filesystem-related component being installed does not establish reachability under Glyph's policy.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: NetFSFramework race enabling sandbox escape; addressed in Sequoia 15.7.

cves.applicability_note: Confused-deputy precedent. Review permitted service relationships; the advisory alone does not establish a usable service route from this sandbox.
cves.component_and_version_scope_at_review: SharedFileList permissions flaw enabling sandbox escape; addressed in Sequoia 15.7.
